english.title: Producer / distributor fail to give notice to enforcement authority of risks of product placed on market / supplied
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being the

(A)_[producer]_
(B)_[distributor]_

of a product, namely **(..SPECIFY PRODUCT..), you had

(C)_[placed on the market]_
(D)_[supplied]_

and which you ought to have known to pose risks to consumers that were incompatible with the general safety requirement, failed to give a notice to **(..SPECIFY AUTHORITY..) the enforcement authority, under regulation 9(1) of the General Product Safety Regulations 2005
english.legislation: Contrary to regulation 20(3) of the General Product Safety Regulations 2005.

other.penalty:
Summary: Three months imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
A magistrates' court may try an information in respect of an offence under these Regulations if the information is laid within three years from the date of the offence or within one year from the discovery of the offence by the prosecutor whichever is the earlier (regulation 41).

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
